questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests must cover distributed transactions with asynchronous callbacks, idempotency keys to avoid duplicates across retries, and cross-region consistency. This mirrors real-world retail/back-office systems at Lyft/Goldman Sachs.

## Key Concepts
- Distributed async workflows
- Idempotency, exactly-once vs at-least-once
- Partial failure simulation (downstream outages)
- Data reconciliation and tombstones
- Latency budgets and observability (SLIs)

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo-idempotent processor
function processCheckoutEvent(event, store) {
  const key = event.idempotencyKey;
  if (store.has(key)) return store.get(key); // idempotent
  const res = doWork(event); // triggers downstream
  store.set(key, res);
  return res;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you structure a test to verify exactly-once semantics when events can be delivered multiple times?
- What metrics and dashboards would you use to detect latency regressions in the downstream flow during peak load?

## Why This Is Asked

- Webhook replay protection

const resp2 = await api.post('/orders', {symbol:'AAPL', qty:1}, {headers:{'Idempotency-Key': key}});
console.assert(resp2.status === 200 && resp2.body.id === resp1.body.id);

## Why This Is Asked
This evaluates understanding of idempotent API design, asynchronous workflows, and comprehensive testing strategies in distributed systems.

- Idempotency keys prevent duplicate operations
- Asynchronous job processing and status polling
- Input validation and error response design
- Concurrent request handling and race conditions
- Test isolation and data management
- Tooling selection for different testing phases

## Code Example
```javascript
// Jest test example
const payload = {cart: [{id: 'p1', qty: 2}], currency: 'USD'}
const headers = {'Idempotency-Key': 'abc-123'}

const response1 = await request(app)
  .post('/checkout')
  .set(headers)
  .send(payload)
  .expect(202)

const response2 = await request(app)
  .post('/checkout')
  .set(headers)
  .send(payload)
  .expect(200)

expect(response1.body.jobId).toBe(response2.body.jobId)
```

## Why This Is Asked

- End-to-end testing of asynchronous workflows
- Idempotency and exactly-once delivery
- Webhook retry logic and compensating actions
- Eventual consistency under partial outages

```javascript
// Pseudo-test: ensure same idempotency key yields single order
const res1 = await post('/orders', { items:[{id:1,qty:2}], idempotencyKey:'abc-123' });
const res2 = await post('/orders', { items:[{id:1,qty:2}], idempotencyKey:'abc-123' });
assert(res1.data.orderId === res2.data.orderId);
```
